headline: High risk is limited by non-runnable docs-only profiles, but Superset’s allowlisted egress creates medium leakage and conflict pathways if paired in a shared workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable course repo with no shared channel documented, while agent B exposes only a Superset API and allowlisted egress. A prompt-injection path is not evidenced by default, but if outputs are manually copied into B or a shared workspace is introduced, content could be misread as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF operator manually copies A-generated text into B prompts or API payloads
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into B prompts
Add a fixed instruction prefix that ignores embedded directives
Review any A-produced text before feeding it to B
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A has no documented data classes touched and no egress, but agent B has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API surface. If they share a workspace or A’s files are fed into B, B can transmit those contents outward. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default BI workflows, though the exact shared-storage setup is not documented.
conditions: IF A and B share a filesystem or exported dataset
IF B is configured to ingest files produced by A
mitigations: Store A and B artifacts in separate directories
Restrict B to synthetic or redacted inputs
Audit outbound API destinations for B
Remove sensitive columns before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces documented, while B exposes only a Superset API and allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of overlapping filesystem, git, or database writes, so direct capability conflict is not established. Uncertainty remains because A’s io_surfaces are empty and the pair is unverified, so the safer low severity is appropriate.
conditions: IF A is later given write access to the same mutable resource as B
IF B is granted filesystem or git write privileges not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep B API-only for shared resources
Avoid granting A write permissions
Document any shared mutable targets
Use separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add locking for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course/repo artifact and B is a BI tool with an API, so a workflow where A’s outputs are treated as authoritative inputs to B is plausible. Because B can act on API-driven content, unverified A outputs could cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. The pathway is inferred rather than directly observed, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced text, SQL, or configuration without validation
IF B renders or executes A-derived artifacts as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A outputs
Validate schemas and queries from A
Use test datasets for A-to-B handoff
Log and diff all imported artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile shows PHI, EU PII, residency constraints, retention policies, or regulated secrets. A is a docs-only open-source course repo and B is an open-source Superset profile with no secrets handled. With no compliance-sensitive data class documented, a residency or certification mismatch is not evidenced.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF residency or retention requirements are added to the deployment
mitigations: Classify data before use
Document retention settings
Avoid regulated data in this pair
Review deployment residency
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
